skill.name: product-decision-agent
skill.description: A Chinese-language product decision assistant for mainland China internet teams. It diagnoses product, growth, operations, data, delivery, and stakeholder problems, then recommends prioritized actions, metrics, and stop conditions.
skill.summary: Diagnose product problems and turn incomplete evidence into prioritized, measurable next steps in Chinese.
skill.author: atdy

content.value_statement: Product teams often act on symptoms, incomplete data, or stakeholder pressure. This skill identifies the main blockage and produces focused actions, metrics, and stop conditions.
actual_capabilities: Diagnoses product, growth, operations, data, delivery, and collaboration problems in Chinese.
Separates provided facts from assumptions and identifies evidence that could change the decision.
Prioritizes one main blockage instead of listing equally weighted options.
Recommends actions with time windows, owners, metrics, and decision rules.
Suggests experiments, rollback conditions, and work that should stop.
Adapts guidance to product stages from exploration through crisis response.
limitations: It cannot access analytics, customer records, project tools, or live market data unless the user provides them.
Recommendations depend on the accuracy and completeness of the supplied context.
It does not execute product changes, experiments, communications, or organizational decisions.
Its default guidance targets mainland China internet product teams and may need localization elsewhere.

use_cases.title: Prioritize a crowded roadmap
use_cases.description: Identify the result that matters most, rank competing requests, and define what the team should stop.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a metric decline
use_cases.description: Break a growth or retention change into likely contribution segments and create a short investigation plan.

use_cases.title: Resolve stakeholder pressure
use_cases.description: Compare delivery options, expose tradeoffs, and set escalation or rollback criteria for conflicting commitments.

prompt_templates.title: Basic product diagnosis
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this product problem in Chinese: [problem]. State the real blockage, three actions, one risk, and the evidence I should confirm.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this when the problem is clear but the next step is uncertain.

prompt_templates.title: Roadmap prioritization
prompt_templates.prompt: We have [team capacity], [candidate items], [goal], and [deadline]. Prioritize the work, explain tradeoffs, name what to stop, and define success metrics.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this to choose work for a constrained release or planning cycle.

prompt_templates.title: Metric change investigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Our [metric] changed from [baseline] to [current] over [period]. Separate facts from assumptions, segment likely causes, and propose a 48-hour investigation plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for retention, conversion, traffic, revenue, or operational anomalies.

prompt_templates.title: Stakeholder decision design
prompt_templates.prompt: A stakeholder requests [request] while the team is committed to [objective]. Build decision options with costs, owners, reversibility, escalation criteria, and stop conditions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use this for high-pressure, multi-constraint decisions with organizational consequences.

output_examples.input: Our community DAU fell 15 percent for two weeks. Operations wants a promotion immediately.
output_examples.output: Problem judgment: Do not start with a promotion. First identify whether the decline comes from acquisition, returning users, content supply, distribution, or a release. Within 24 hours, segment the decline and inspect the largest contributor. Restart promotion only after the main retention or supply issue is controlled.

output_examples.input: An executive wants a loyalty marketplace next week, but the release is focused on new-user conversion.
output_examples.output: Problem judgment: This is a resource conflict between two release goals. Present three options: protect the current goal, run a two-day marketplace validation, or replace named conversion work. Record the displaced scope, owner, deadline impact, and success rule before committing.

best_practices: Provide the current goal, baseline metric, time window, affected user group, and recent changes.
State hard constraints such as staffing, budget, deadline, permissions, and contractual commitments.
Report new evidence after the first action so the skill can revise the recommendation.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for a strategy without sharing the target result or current evidence.
Do not treat recommendations as verified facts when the input contains only opinions.
Do not request a broad option list when the real need is a prioritized decision.

faq.question: What language does this skill use?
faq.answer: It answers in Chinese by default and keeps necessary product abbreviations in English.

faq.question: Can it prioritize product requirements?
faq.answer: Yes. It connects requests to goals, constraints, opportunity costs, evidence, and the current product stage.

faq.question: Can it analyze live product data?
faq.answer: No. Provide relevant metrics, segments, dates, definitions, and recent changes in the prompt.

faq.question: Does it create complete PRDs?
faq.answer: It can clarify the problem, decision, scope, metrics, and risks. Detailed specifications still require product and engineering input.

faq.question: Can it resolve team conflicts automatically?
faq.answer: No. It can map stakeholders, incentives, costs, decision rights, and practical alignment options.

faq.question: How should I validate its recommendation?
faq.answer: Run the smallest useful test, track the stated metric and guardrails, then revise the decision with new evidence.
